source.title: Attend Who is Weak: Pruning-assisted Medical Image Localization under Sophisticated and Implicit Imbalances
source.authors: Ajay Jaiswal; Tian-Long Chen; Justin F. Rousseau; Yi-Fan Peng; Ying Ding; Zhangyang Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Uses pruning as a tool to identify hard-to-learn localization examples, relying on prior work about pruning and memorization. It does not test fitting random labels or the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports pruning-induced changes in foreground/background localization and uses those changes to mine hard-to-learn examples. These results concern a related pruning/forgetting construct, not any listed claim version; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Baseline comparisons of the proposed HTL fine-tuning method are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures pruning sensitivity and localization improvements on medical images with ordinary labels or pseudo-labels. It cites pattern-first learning as background but neither tests nor operationally uses random-label fitting or real-versus-noisy-label learning dynamics. Its pruning results concern a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that pruning identifies hard-to-learn localization examples, attending to these examples during fine-tuning improves localization, and demographic analyses suggest that the mined examples reveal implicit demographic imbalances.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pruning to identify sensitive localization examples, then fine-tunes with attention to them; it does not reproduce random-label training.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning ratio and pruning method change the measured foreground IoU drop; supervised and semi-supervised settings also show different percentage drops.

fits_no_version.finding: Magnitude-based pruning reduces foreground training IoU more than background training IoU across the reported supervised and semi-supervised conditions. At 70% pruning, approximately 18% of instances lose at least 40% foreground IoU, compared with approximately 1% for background.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning trained localization networks can disproportionately impair foreground localization relative to background localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Foreground IoU decreases under random, unstructured magnitude-based, and structured magnitude-based pruning, with larger losses at higher sparsity. Table 3 reports no background values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Foreground localization performance depends on pruning method and sparsity.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The reported pruning analyses concern localization IoU, not fitting random labels or generalization under random labels. Several effects are given as aggregate drops; the text does not provide uncertainty for Table 1 or Table 3.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 results comparing the proposed HTL-aware fine-tuning method with baselines are omitted because they evaluate the paper's proposed training method rather than the claim's random-label fitting or related pruning-induced forgetting behavior.

untested.parts: All parts: random-label training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
All parts: relative fitting time and convergence across label-corruption fractions.
All parts: fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
All parts: perfect training fit and test-error degradation across random-label corruption fractions.
All parts: whether regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
All parts: temporal ordering of real-pattern learning and noisy-label memorization. Pruning sensitivity after training does not measure this ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The observed pruning effects are valid findings outside these versions; cannot_determine describes their inability to measure the specified claims. Random pruning randomizes weight removal, not labels. Pseudo-label use does not supply a controlled test of random-label memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and generalization on true labels.
Training time and convergence as label corruption changes.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test performance across corruption fractions.
Effects of regularization or augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
